why_math: Long documents repeat ideas across sentences; models learn that certain early patterns (topic words, repeated themes) predict what summaries will mention, so they copy and compress those phrases.

math_plain: Creates a tamper-evident log where each video segment gets a unique cryptographic fingerprint recorded on blockchain, making edits detectable.
why_math: Hashes change completely if any bit changes; once logged publicly, anyone can recompute a video's hash and compare it to the log, instantly catching tampering. The math exploits one-way functions—easy to compute, impossible to reverse.

math_plain: Identifies which user behaviors truly cause others (view leads to buy) versus which happen together by chance, then weights each chain by causal strength.
why_math: Confounders like sales make unrelated things appear linked; causal inference filters these out by asking 'what would happen if we broke this link?' revealing true cause-effect. Real causes explain behavior chains better than coincidence.

why_math: Language has hidden structure (word order, grammar rules) that constrains meaning; injecting these patterns early creates a robust foundation. Feedback-guided curriculum focuses on hard examples, avoiding wasted effort on easy ones.

math_plain: Predicts which parts of long documents the model will actually need to read, then loads only those parts instead of storing everything in memory.
why_math: Attention over long texts is sparse—the model only looks at a few important parts. Predicting which parts matter ahead of time saves memory; the model can still understand the full meaning from key pieces.
